[head=2][color=#ff7f7f]Taypani Free Stations Coalition[/color][/head]
The Coalition, or TFSC, is one of the few powers actually native to Taypan. It is a company of pirate crews, mercenary cells, shipbreakers, and seedy corporations bound together by profit rather than by any flag. Most of the galaxy considers it illegitimate, yet it is the largest independent power in the entire system, with motherships and stations of its own.
There is no crown and no bloodline here. In the Coalition [bold]strength and results decide everything[/bold], so the crew that hits hardest and earns the most sits at the top. Gorlex Security Consulting (GSC) is its most numerous armed cell, feared for boarding actions and heists across the sector.
[head=3][color=#ff7f7f]Leadership[/color][/head]
- [bold]Ringleader.[/bold] The boss of a cell, in charge by force of will and reputation. - [bold]Lieutenant.[/bold] The Ringleader's second, running the crew day to day. - [bold]Patriarch.[/bold] An intelligence and network figure who pulls strings behind the scenes.
[head=3][color=#ff7f7f]Crew[/color][/head]
- [bold]Gorlex Infanteer.[/bold] The standard pirate trooper and boarder. - [bold]Newblood.[/bold] A fresh recruit or technician still proving their worth. - [bold]Ripperdoc.[/bold] The crew's back-alley surgeon and cybernetics fitter.
[head=3][color=#ff7f7f]Member Companies[/color][/head]
- [bold]Cyberdawn.[/bold] A tech and munitions firm supplying hardlight weaponry, staffed by Asset Security and Researchers. - [bold]Interdyne.[/bold] Corporate handlers who coordinate operations through their Coordinators. - [bold]SAW.[/bold] The Shipfitters and Astronautics Workers, breakers and haulers turned privateers. - [bold]TraumaSec.[/bold] Hired security muscle brought in when a job needs guns.
[head=3][color=#ff7f7f]How to address them[/color][/head]
Keep it [bold]casual[/bold]. The one in charge is the [color=#ff7f7f][bold]Captain[/bold][/color] or the [color=#ff7f7f][bold]Boss[/bold][/color], or is addressed by rank as Ringleader or Patriarch. Crewmates go by name or nickname.
Titles and stiff formality are [color=#d9776c]mocked[/color] rather than respected. Try to call a pirate captain "My Lord" and you will get laughed at, if you are lucky. See the [color=#e8b04b]Forms of Address[/color] page for more.
